desc: Implement `canAchieve(L)`: scan string left-to-right, tracking the current run length of the same character; when adding a character would make the run length `L+1`, flip the current character (increment flips) and reset run length to 1; return `flips <= numOps`.
In `minLength`, binary search `L` over `[1, n]` to find the minimum feasible `L` using `canAchieve`, and return the resulting `lo`.
Handle edge cases: `numOps = 0` (return original max run length), `n = 1` (return 1), and `numOps >= n` (return 1 for `n >= 2`).
Add quick sanity tests for the three given examples inside an `if __name__ == "__main__":` block.
(Optional but recommended) Add a brute-force verifier for `n <= 10` to confirm greedy correctness on random strings and random `numOps` values.
